editorial:
Imagine spending your whole life just doing what other people tell you to do. That is exactly where you find Sawada. He is a talented art student who ended up as a glorified helper for a famous artist, losing his own spark along the way. The movie feels very quiet and calm at first, but things take a weird turn when an accident costs him his job and leaves him with a hurt arm. Stuck at home and feeling lost, he spots a tiny ant on the floor and follows its movement to draw a simple circle. This small act starts a strange chain reaction that slowly changes his entire world, making you wonder if he is finally waking up or just losing his mind.

What really works here is how the movie shows a man finding himself through something as simple as a shape. The acting is subtle, and the pacing is slow, which might feel boring if you want a big action movie, but it is perfect for a rainy afternoon. You will appreciate the soft colors and the peaceful mood.
endingExplained: In the end, Sawada stops living for others and starts creating for himself. The circle becomes a way for him to reclaim his identity and his love for art. He moves past his sadness and the fear of failure. The movie wraps up with him finding a new sense of peace and purpose, showing that even a small, random moment can lead to a big life change and a fresh start.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slow stories about personal growth and art.
